newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks reverse early gains on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks reverse early gains on profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks reversed mid-session gains after profit-taking on Wednesday to close down 6.29 points or 0.19 percent at 3,302.98 points.
"You could tell dealers wanted to take profits when stocks were up, as many stocks prices were high," one trader said.
Analysts cited caution among dealers ahead of U.S. economic data due on Thursday
"Here they were more concerned than in the U.S. over producer price figures," an analyst said. "Even gains on the Dow Jones didn't convice them nothing bad will happen."
Volume was lackluster at 71.7 million shares traded.
Some dealers said market sentiment was affected by expectations of a sharp rebound in primary Cetes, or Treasury bill, rates next week after Tuesday's auction results were lower than expected.
A total of 106 stocks were traded, and gainers outnumbered losers 45 to 36.
Sidek L series headed the percentage leaders with a gain of 50 percent to three pesos (40 cents) after trading for the first time since August 28.
"What happened with Sidek is that it had been revalued in the U.S. but had not traded here. It's just catching up with the market," an analyst said.
Financial group Invermexico grabbed attention as all four of its share series gained sharply. The LCP series closed 11 percent up at 1.11 pesos (15 cents)
Analysts said Invermexico was boosted by rumours of a possible association with a foreign bank. Plus, it had lagged behind the market as its shares are not frequently traded.

Beverage company Emvasa B series led the percentage losers after a fall of 5.17 percent to 5.50 pesos (73 cents), but at a relatively low volume of 26,000 shares traded. The day's second-greatest fall was chalked up by steelmaker Hylsamex's BCP series, which closed 3.83 percent down at 30.10 pesos on 582,000 shares traded.
